correctness.rationale: Full proof checked for N≥4 and arbitrary nonnegative weights: a semicircle first-moment obstruction rules out D<N/2; at odd D=(N+1)/2 a cubic polynomial x(x²−a²), combining only first/third harmonics, is nonnegative at all allowed nodes and positive on every interior node, so no nonzero quadrature is possible; even antipodal and odd explicit three-cosine-level positive mass constructions satisfy both complex moments with endpoint support. The N=5 duplicated central index is handled by merging weights. The standalone program executed 997 grid tests, 1994 complex moment comparisons, and six rational algebraic identity checks; these corroborate but do not prove the infinite theorem.

evidence: Peherstorfer (arXiv:1001.2451v1), sections 2 and 3, characterizes positive quadratures for complete low-degree Laurent polynomial spaces, with nodes not confined to the problem-specific consecutive cyclic window.
Kunis (arXiv:2608.11915), introduction and Theorem 3.3, gives geometric covering bounds for positive full-degree trigonometric quadrature, and construction of sampling curves.
An (arXiv:2610.11814v1), sections 2–3, proves regular full-grid equal-weight exactness and projects it to Gauss–Chebyshev quadrature.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The available general full-degree exactness theorems do not imply this exact sparse {1,3}-moment aperture law, because omitting the even second harmonic changes the feasible measures and the optimal aperture; the full-grid theorem has no restricted-window optimization.

originality.rationale: Searches of mathematical records, accessible own claim summaries, and material readings of three primary arXiv manuscripts and two directly same-harmonic published mathematical records did not identify a covering theorem. The closest problems differ at the level of exactness band, support geometry, and optimization variables. Significant historical-priority uncertainty remains; absence of an indexed match does not certify uniqueness.
residual_risks: Older sparse trigonometric quadrature or finite cyclic moment-cone treatments may contain equivalent formulations under unfamiliar terminology.

The published full-grid polynomial results are dual-adjacent but their stated objectives do not settle the moving-arc support threshold; undiscovered consequences have not been exhaustively ruled out.
No independent scholarly refereeing or scientific validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The first and third frequencies form the first two odd modes of the natural translation-invariant odd trigonometric subspace. The exact consecutive cyclic aperture is a geometrically intrinsic invariant; the theorem solves it completely for all grid orders, isolates the sharp odd-grid overshoot beyond the semicircle obstruction, and supplies uniform positive at-most-six-node constructions. These are structurally motivated and not merely parameter substitutions or a finite table.
